source.title: Entropy-SGD optimizes the prior of a PAC-Bayes bound: Generalization properties of Entropy-SGD and data-dependent priors

record.tranche_reason: The study tests training and test error on natural and random labels, and shows that generalization depends strongly on thermal noise and the algorithm; Entropy-SGD can overfit random labels, while its privacy-tuned variant avoids it with weaker natural-label performance.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the study's own reported outcomes on natural and random labels, including optimizer and thermal-noise conditions and the stated width comparison. Detailed values shown only in figures are not reconstructed. Cited results from other studies are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own natural-label and fixed-random-label training results bearing on V1, and convolutional versus fully connected test errors bearing on V3, in new architecture and optimizer settings. Its critique of Entropy-SGD's generalization guarantees does not itself challenge any listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate. Entropy-SGD optimizes a PAC-Bayes prior using the training data, invalidating the ordinary bound, and can rapidly fit random labels. Adding outer-loop noise yields Entropy-SGLD, which can fit natural labels while suppressing random-label overfitting. Its empirical bounds assume convergence and omit the convergence correction; despite tighter bounds, learning is slower and test performance remains worse than SGD and state of the art.
record.recipe_differences: Studies SGD, SGLD, Entropy-SGD, and a modified Entropy-SGLD algorithm with added outer-loop noise; uses bounded cross-entropy and evaluates two-class MNIST and CIFAR10, including random labels. It does not reproduce the listed original studies' full model and training settings.
record.method_sensitivity: Thermal noise, τ, γ, data-label distribution, and architecture affect reported risk or generalization outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: FC600 and FC1200 have similar training errors and generalization gaps under private Entropy-SGLD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing fully connected width can leave error approximately unchanged under this private training recipe; this does not establish behavior beyond interpolation.

fits_no_version.finding: Entropy-SGD optimizes a data-dependent PAC-Bayes prior, and the Entropy-SGLD bounds omit a convergence correction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Validity and usefulness of these generalization certificates depend on prior construction and convergence assumptions.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), Proceedings of the 35th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 80, 2018
record.problems: The Entropy-SGLD PAC-Bayes bounds are optimistic because the authors assume SGLD has converged and omit the additional convergence term. Exact plotted errors are not consistently stated in prose. Monte Carlo error is not accounted for in one PAC-Bayes bound estimate. The authors note possible MNIST test-set overfitting for one comparison.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Detailed figure-only values and additional CIFAR10 parameter-sweep values were not transcribed because the text does not give them numerically.

untested.parts: The original CIFAR-10 architectures and ImageNet setting are not reproduced. Near-perfect random-label fitting is not numerically established for every optimizer/noise condition, and the fully connected binary-MNIST experiments lack matching random-label runs.
No width sweep establishes zero training error and then measures test error beyond that width; the two private fully connected models retain training error.

The contribution of local connectivity, learned sparse local connections, and convolutional initialization of fully connected models are not isolated. The reported architecture comparison uses Entropy-SGLD.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparison or tuning-budget experiment.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets.
No dropout ablation; omitting dropout is not a test of its effect.
No magnitude-scaled sharpness ranking against generalization gaps or comparison with norm and margin measures.
No identification or removal of memorized examples followed by retraining.

missing.what: Explicit zero random-label training error for available Entropy-SGD implementations and their Gibbs posteriors, paired with the low-noise natural-label results.
Ten-class MNIST natural/random-label outcomes for FC1024 and CONV, including random-label errors near chance and the small residual overfitting.
Ten-class MNIST architecture comparison: CONV has lower training and test error than FC1024.

Qualitative natural-label CIFAR-10 test error below 0.3 at high τ, needed to pair R11's random-label fitting with useful natural-label performance. This is explicitly stated in the caption, not merely an unread plotted value.

record.verdict_notes: Generalization error in this study usually means a training–population error gap, not held-out classification error. Random-label overfitting is evidence for memorization in V1, not evidence against it. The width comparison does not test V2, and no result tests magnitude-aware sharpness in V7.

versions.untested_parts: The listed small Inception, AlexNet, and MLP settings on CIFAR-10 and Inception V3 on ImageNet are not tested; the study uses two-class MNIST and CIFAR-10.

The tested FC600 and FC1200 comparison is a three-layer network comparison, not a one-hidden-layer ReLU width sweep past the zero-training-error threshold; it reports similar rather than decreasing errors.
No fully connected network learning sparse local connections or convolutionally initialized fully connected network is tested.
Batch size is not varied as a condition for the claim.
Dropout is not varied; the authors state they do not use dropout.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with norm- or margin-based measures are not measured.
Memorized examples are not identified, removed, or retrained upon.

rows.subject: CONV
rows.operation_detail: Train with SGD on true labels and measure training and test error.
rows.measure: Training and test 0–1 error; generalization error
rows.value: SGD achieves the smallest training and test error on true labels.
rows.note: Exact errors are not stated in the text.
rows.check: Records the natural-label component of V1; interpret jointly with the random-label condition R2. Exact errors are not supplied in prose.

source_check.locator_found: Section 5.2; Figure 1 caption; Appendix C architecture description.

rows.subject: CONV
rows.operation_detail: Train with SGD on random labels and measure generalization error.
rows.value: SGD overfits the worst on random labels.
rows.note: The text does not give the exact training or test error.
rows.check: The prose establishes strong random-label overfitting, but does not quantify near-perfect training fit for this SGD condition. Figure 1 states that random-label population error is 50%; generalization error here means the train–population gap.

rows.subject: CONV
rows.operation_detail: Train with SGLD at 0.05 thermal noise on true and random labels.
rows.value: SGLD achieves reasonable but relatively large risk but almost zero generalization error on both true and random labels.
rows.note: The text does not state exact risk or error values.
rows.check: Split true and random labels into separate rows. Almost zero generalization gap on random labels means little memorization, not successful prediction of random labels; natural-label risk is relatively large.

source_check.locator_found: Section 5.2, discussion of Figure 1 left column.

rows.subject: CONV
rows.operation_detail: Train with Entropy-SGD at 0.01 thermal noise on true and random labels.
rows.value: Entropy-SGD achieves good risk and low generalization error on both true and random labels; its test-set performance at 0.01 thermal noise is still worse than SGD.
rows.note: Exact risk and error values are not stated.
rows.check: Split true and random labels. Good natural-label performance and little random-label overfitting do not establish the near-perfect random-label fit required by V1.

source_check.locator_found: Section 5.2, discussion of Figure 1 middle column.

rows.subject: CONV
rows.operation_detail: Train with Entropy-SGD at the stated low thermal-noise settings on random labels.
rows.value: Entropy-SGD overfits for thermal noise values 0.005 and below.
rows.note: The caption identifies overfitting at these settings; exact error values are figure-only.
rows.check: This is the random-label memorization component, not a limitation of V1. The abstract additionally states that available Entropy-SGD implementations rapidly reach zero random-label training error, including the Gibbs posterior; the caption alone does not establish zero error at every listed noise value.

rows.subject: CONV
rows.operation_detail: Train with Entropy-SGLD at τ = √m on true labels and evaluate the mean and Gibbs classifiers.
rows.value: Both the mean and Gibbs classifier have approximately 2% test error and essentially zero generalization error.
rows.check: Establishes the natural-label accuracy component only. Split mean and Gibbs classifiers into separate rows; neither this result nor a small generalization gap establishes random-label memorization.

source_check.locator_found: Section 5.2, discussion of Figure 1 right column.

rows.subject: CONV
rows.operation_detail: Train with Entropy-SGLD at τ = √m on random labels for thousands of epochs.
rows.value: Entropy-SGLD, properly tuned, does not overfit on random labels, even after thousands of epochs.
rows.note: The explicit statement concerns overfitting; exact errors are not stated.
rows.check: Random-label memorization is absent under this privacy-tuned recipe. This qualifies extension to this recipe rather than refuting coexistence under SGD.

rows.subject: FC600
rows.operation_detail: Train with Entropy-SGLD on true labels and compare train and test error.
rows.measure: Training error, test error, and generalization gap
rows.value: Training and generalization error are similar to FC1200; the true generalization gap is close to zero.
rows.note: The caption reports the comparison in prose.
rows.check: Only natural labels are tested for this architecture. Similar errors across two widths with nonzero training error do not test widening beyond the zero-training-error threshold in V2.

rows.subject: FC1200
rows.operation_detail: Train with Entropy-SGLD on true labels and compare train and test error with FC600.
rows.measure: Training error, test error, and generalization gap
rows.baseline: FC600: both training error and generalization error are similar.
rows.value: Both training error and generalization error are similar for FC600 and FC1200; the true generalization gap is close to zero.
rows.note: The authors report similar errors despite FC1200 having three times as many parameters.
rows.check: Neither random-label memorization nor a width comparison beyond a demonstrated interpolation threshold is measured. The reported parameter counts imply about 2.86 times as many parameters; three times is approximate.

rows.subject: CONV
rows.operation_detail: Train with Entropy-SGLD on true labels and measure generalization gap.
rows.value: For true-label data, the generalization error does not exceed 0.2.
rows.note: The text states the bound on generalization error but does not provide exact values by τ.
rows.check: A generalization gap at most 0.2 alone establishes neither low natural-label training error nor accuracy above chance. Appendix E.1 places this statement in the regime τ > 10^5; add the natural-label test-error result from Figure 5.

source_check.locator_found: Appendix E.1, discussion of Figure 5 top row.

rows.subject: CONV
rows.operation_detail: Train with Entropy-SGLD on random labels and measure generalization error across τ.
rows.value: The size of the generalization gap appears to be data distribution dependent; on random labels with large true Bayes error, the classifier can achieve almost zero classification error, resulting in maximal generalization error.
rows.note: The prose describes the trend and its distribution dependence; precise values are figure-only.
rows.check: Almost zero classification error refers to training error. Distinguish the transition around 10^4–10^5 from maximal overfitting, which Figure 5 places at τ > 10^6 for γ = 0.03. Record the test/chance error separately.

source_check.correct: For β = 1 and γ = 0.03, Appendix E.1 discusses distribution-dependent gaps above τ = 10^5; Figure 5 specifies maximal random-label overfitting at τ > 10^6. Almost-zero classification error refers to training error.
source_check.problem: The stated τ range is too broad for the maximal-overfitting endpoint; distinguish it from the transition and distribution-dependent regime.

rows.subject: CONV
rows.operation_detail: Train convolutional and fully connected architectures with Entropy-SGLD on true labels and compare errors.
rows.baseline: FC600 and FC1200: their results are nearly identical to one another.
rows.value: Training the CONV network produces the lowest training and test errors and tightest generalization bounds.
rows.note: The comparison is reported in prose; the text does not give exact error values.
rows.check: Supports the architecture comparison under Entropy-SGLD. Generalization-bound tightness is a separate measure and should not be combined with test error.

relationships.condition: CONV trained with SGD on binary MNIST
relationships.reason: R1 reports small natural-label training and test errors, while R2 reports strong random-label overfitting with 50% population error; this supports coexistence qualitatively, although near-perfect random-label fit is not quantified in prose.
relationships.display_finding: Natural-label errors were small, whereas random labels produced strong overfitting and 50% population error, without a quantified training endpoint.

relationships.condition: Binary MNIST with SGLD noise 0.05, Entropy-SGD noise 0.01, or privacy-tuned Entropy-SGLD
relationships.reason: R3–R4 and R6–R7 show that recipes retaining natural-label performance can suppress random-label memorization, so coexistence does not extend to all tested noise and privacy settings.
